events.body:
The rider disputes the $6.61 cancellation fee after the driver cancelled, claiming she came out a minute later. The fee is chargeable only through NS-0, and since `cancelled_by = driver` with the driver asserting a rider no-show, the case runs on NS-1 / NS-2 only [F4][NS-0].

NS-1 requires all three conditions. (i) The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:56:20 [F6]. (ii) At that moment GPS put him 40 m from the pickup point (closest approach overall 38 m), i.e. inside the 200 m arrival radius [F6][F1]. (iii) He then stayed within the radius for 3 min 5 s before cancelling at 09:59:25 — more than the required 3 minutes [F6][F3][F4]. Independently, the platform recorded arrival at 09:54:55 with 4 min 30 s within 200 m before cancellation [F5][F2]. The chat corroborates: at 09:56 the driver announces his position and car, and at 09:59 cancels stating he waited more than 3 minutes [F9][F10][F11]. The driver's written statement is consistent but is a statement, not established consent or a verdict; the finding rests on the system records, which take priority [F12][F1][F2][F3][F6].

Because NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) all hold, the $6.61 cancellation fee is properly charged and no refund is due under NS-2 [F7][NS-1][NS-2]. The rider's "one minute late" account does not change the assessment: the chargeable event is the driver's arrival and 3-minute wait, both recorded, not the rider's appearance time [F2][F6][NS-1]. The rider's only route to relief would be the 30-day human fee-waiver process, which is Ryde's discretion and not a ground to overturn the fee here [NS-7]. No fare overcharge arises: this is a fixed-quote RydeX trip and the only disputed item is the published cancellation fee [F7][F8][FARE-1].
